cuebot.pollStarted.description: Runs when a chat poll starts. Good for announcing the question and how to vote in chat.

variables.title: The poll's question
variables.choice0Title: The first choice's text (choice1Title is the second, and so on)
variables.duration: How many seconds the poll lasts (0 = until you end it)

cuebot.pollEnded.description: Runs when a chat poll ends. Good for announcing which choice won.

variables.title: The poll's question
variables.winningChoice: The text of the winning choice (empty if nobody voted)
variables.winningVotes: How many votes the winner got
variables.totalVotes: How many votes there were in all
variables.choice0Title: The first choice's text (choice1Title is the second, and so on)
variables.choice0Votes: How many votes the first choice got (choice1Votes is the second, and so on)
variables.canceled: True if the poll was cancelled

cuebot.predictionStarted.description: Runs when a chat prediction opens for bets. Viewers bet their points on what will happen. Good for announcing the question.

variables.title: The prediction's question
variables.outcome0Title: The first outcome's text (outcome1Title is the second, and so on)
variables.window: How many seconds bets are taken (0 = until you lock it)
variables.currency: The name of the points that are bet

cuebot.predictionLocked.description: Runs when a chat prediction is locked, so no more bets are taken. Good for saying "bets are closed".

variables.title: The prediction's question
variables.totalPoints: How many points were bet in all
variables.outcome0Points: Points bet on the first outcome (outcome1Points is the second, and so on)
variables.currency: The name of the points that were bet

cuebot.predictionResolved.description: Runs when you pick the winning outcome of a prediction and the winners get paid. Good for announcing the result.

variables.title: The prediction's question
variables.winningOutcome: The text of the winning outcome
variables.paidOut: How many points were paid out in all
variables.totalPoints: How many points were bet in all

cuebot.predictionCanceled.description: Runs when a prediction is cancelled and every bet is given back. Good for telling chat that the points are back.

variables.title: The prediction's question
variables.totalPoints: How many points are given back in all

cuebot.giveawayOpened.description: Runs when a giveaway opens for entries. Good for announcing the prize and how to join.

variables.title: The prize
variables.command: The chat command to join, like !join
variables.ticketCost: How many points one ticket costs (0 = free)
variables.maxTickets: The most tickets one viewer may get
variables.duration: How many seconds entries are taken (0 = until you close it)

cuebot.giveawayEntered.description: Runs each time a viewer joins a giveaway. Good for a quick "you're in!" reply.

variables.tickets: How many tickets they hold now
variables.added: How many tickets they just got
variables.title: The prize
variables.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch

cuebot.giveawayClosed.description: Runs when a giveaway stops taking entries, by hand or when the time is up. Good for saying "no more entries" before the draw.

variables.title: The prize
variables.tickets: How many tickets there are in all

cuebot.giveawayWinner.description: Runs once for each winner drawn in a giveaway. Good for a big congratulations alert.

variables.winnerPlatform: The site the winner is on, like twitch
variables.winnerTickets: How many tickets the winner had
variables.title: The prize

cuebot.giveawayCanceled.description: Runs when a giveaway is cancelled and the points for tickets are given back.

variables.title: The prize
variables.refunded: How many points were given back in all

quotes.added.description: Runs when a new quote is saved. Good for a chat reply like "Quote #12 added!".

fields.user: Only react to quotes by this person, like "kris". Empty means every quote.

variables.quoteGame: The game or category at the time

quotes.updated.description: Runs when a saved quote is edited, for example its text or who said it.

fields.user: Only react to quotes by this person, like "kris". Empty means every quote.

quotes.removed.description: Runs when a quote is deleted.

fields.user: Only react to quotes by this person, like "kris". Empty means every quote.

quotes.shown.description: Runs when a quote is shown to chat, for example by a !quote command. Good for also showing the quote on screen.

fields.user: Only react to quotes by this person, like "kris". Empty means every quote.

variables.quoteGame: The game or category at the time

cuebot.storeRedeemed.description: Runs when a viewer buys something from your points store, and it is approved. Good for doing what the item promises, like playing a sound.

fields.item: The store item's name, exactly as in your store. Empty means any item.

variables.input: Extra text the viewer typed with the purchase
variables.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch

cuebot.storeRejected.description: Runs when a store purchase is turned down and the points are given back. Good for telling the viewer why.

fields.item: The store item's name, exactly as in your store. Empty means any item.

variables.user: The viewer who tried to buy it
variables.cost: How many points are given back

cuebot.storePending.description: Runs when a store purchase is waiting for you to approve it. Good for a popup or sound telling you to check it.

fields.item: The store item's name, exactly as in your store. Empty means any item.

variables.input: Extra text the viewer typed with the purchase
variables.redemptionId: The purchase's internal id (use it with "Approve or reject store redemption")

points.thresholdCrossed.description: Runs when a viewer's points reach a goal number, like 1000. You set the goal numbers on the Points page. Good for a "you reached 1000!" cheer.

fields.threshold: Only react to this goal number, like 1000. Empty means any goal set on the Points page.
fields.currency: Only react to this kind of points, like "Coins". Empty means any.

variables.user: The viewer who reached the goal
variables.threshold: The goal number that was reached
variables.points: How many points they have now
variables.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch

cuebot.mediaRequested.description: Runs when a song or video request is added to the queue. Good for thanking the viewer who requested it.

variables.title: The video's title
variables.author: The channel that made the video
variables.position: Its place in the queue (0 = playing right now)

cuebot.mediaStarted.description: Runs when a requested video starts playing. Good for announcing "now playing" in chat.

variables.title: The video's title
variables.author: The channel that made the video

cuebot.mediaSkipped.description: Runs when a requested video is skipped. Good for a short message in chat.

polls.end.description: Ends the running chat poll now and announces the result. Good if you want to close a poll early or the poll has no time limit.

variables.success: True if a poll was running and was ended
variables.winningChoice: The text of the winning choice
variables.totalVotes: How many votes there were in all

polls.prediction.description: Locks a running prediction so no more bets come in, or picks the winner and pays out, or cancels it and gives all bets back.

fields.mode: Lock = stop taking bets. Resolve = pick the winner and pay out. Cancel = give every bet back.
fields.winner: Only for Resolve: the winning outcome's number (1, 2...) or its text.

variables.winningChoice: Only after Resolve: the text of the winning outcome

polls.start.description: Starts a poll in your chat. Viewers vote by typing the vote command, like !vote 1. Good for "which game next?" moments.

fields.title: The question, like "Which game next?".
fields.choices: The answers to choose from, one per line, 2 to 10 of them. Viewers vote by typing !vote 1, !vote 2 and so on.
fields.duration: How many seconds the poll runs. 0 = until you end it.

polls.startPrediction.description: Starts a prediction: viewers bet their points on what will happen, for example if you win the next round. Needs Cuebot points to be set up.

fields.title: The question, like "Will I win this round?".
fields.outcomes: The possible results, one per line, 2 to 10 of them. Viewers bet by typing !bet 1 500 or !bet 2 all (outcome number, then points).
fields.window: How many seconds viewers can bet. 0 = until you lock the prediction.
fields.currency: The name of the points to bet with, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

giveaways.control.description: Controls the running giveaway: stop taking entries, draw winners, draw one more winner, or cancel it and give points back.

fields.mode: Close entries = nobody else can join. Draw winners = pick the winners. Draw one more = pick another winner. Cancel and refund = stop and give ticket points back.

variables.success: True if there was a giveaway to act on
variables.winners: All winners so far, separated by commas

giveaways.open.description: Opens a giveaway where viewers join by typing a chat command. Later, draw the winners with "Close, draw or cancel giveaway".

fields.title: The prize, like "Steam game key".
fields.command: The chat command viewers type to join, like !join.
fields.ticketCost: How many points one ticket costs. 0 = joining is free.
fields.maxTickets: The most tickets one viewer may have. Viewers buy more by typing !join 3.
fields.currency: The name of the points tickets cost, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.
fields.subscriberLuck: How much better subscribers' tickets count. 2 = each subscriber ticket counts double. 1 = same as everyone.
fields.subscribersOnly: Tick so only subscribers can join.
fields.seconds: How many seconds entries are taken, then it closes by itself. 0 = until you close it.

media.control.description: Controls the song and video request queue: skip the current one, pause, resume, clear the queue, open or close requests, or set the volume.

fields.mode: Skip = next video. Pause/Resume = stop or continue. Clear the queue = remove all waiting requests and give points back. Open/Close requests = allow or block new ones. Set volume = change loudness.
fields.volume: Only for Set volume: how loud, from 0 (silent) to 100 (full).

variables.success: True if it worked (for example, false if there was nothing to skip)
variables.removed: Only for Clear the queue: how many requests were removed

media.request.description: Adds a YouTube video to the request queue from an action, as if a viewer asked. Good for your own "play this" button or command.

fields.link: A YouTube link or the 11-letter video id. The default %rawInput% is what a viewer typed after the command.
fields.user: Who asked for it, shown with the video. The default %user% is whoever started the action.
fields.platform: The site that person is on, like twitch. The default %platform% is whoever started the action.
fields.free: Tick so it costs no points and skips the request rules (requests closed, per-viewer limit). Unticked, the normal rules apply. Leave it ticked for your own actions.

variables.error: If it was not added: the reason, like "that is not a YouTube link"
variables.title: The video's title

credits.addCustom.description: Adds a person to the end credits of your stream, like "Special thanks". Good for thanking someone who does not show up in follows or tips.

fields.section: Which part of the credits. Use a built-in one (follows, tips, raids...) or any title you make up, like "Special thanks".
fields.user: The person's name. The default %user% is whoever started the action.
fields.platform: The site the person is on, like twitch. The default %platform% is whoever started the action.
fields.amount: A number added to the person's total in this section, like a tip amount. 0 if it does not matter.
fields.detail: Optional extra text shown next to the name, like "for the great clip".

credits.get.description: Reads the credits collected so far and saves them in variables, for example the names of all new followers. Handy for a "thanks to everyone" chat message.

fields.test: Tick to use made-up sample credits, for trying out an overlay design.

variables.creditsFollows: The names of all new followers, separated by commas
variables.creditsSubscriptions: The names of everyone who subscribed
variables.creditsTips: The names of everyone who tipped
variables.creditsRaids: The names of everyone who raided
variables.creditsChatters: The names of everyone who chatted
variables.creditsTotal: How many names there are in all

credits.reset.description: Clears the collected credits so the next ones start fresh. Good at the start of a new stream.

overlays.alertQueue.description: Controls the line of alerts on your stream overlay: pause or resume it, skip the alert playing now, or mute alert sounds and videos.

fields.mode: Pause = the alert playing finishes, new ones wait. Resume = go on. Skip = end the playing alert. Mute/Unmute = silence alert sounds and videos. Toggle = switch to the opposite.

variables.alertsPaused: True if the alerts are paused now
variables.alertsMuted: True if the alerts are muted now

overlays.showAlert.description: Shows an alert on your stream overlay yourself, as if someone followed or tipped. Good for testing an alert or making your own with a custom message.

fields.alertType: Which alert design to use: custom, follower, subscriber, tip, cheer, raid, and so on. Pick the one that fits your alert.
fields.name: The name shown in the alert. The default %user% is whoever started the action.
fields.message: The message shown in the alert, if the design has room for one.
fields.amount: A number for the alert, like 5 for a 5 dollar tip. Designs can show different alerts for different amounts.
fields.currency: For money amounts, the currency code, like USD. Empty is fine otherwise.
fields.platform: The site the alert is from: twitch, kick, rumble or youtube. Designs can differ by site.

quotes.add.description: Saves a new quote, with who said it and the game at the time. Good for a !addquote command that saves what a viewer typed.

fields.text: The quote itself. The default %input% is what a viewer typed after the command.
fields.user: Who said it. The default %user% is whoever started the action. Use %input0% to quote someone else.
fields.userId: The speaker's id on their site. Usually leave the default.
fields.platform: The site the speaker is on, like twitch. The default %platform% is whoever started the action.
fields.game: The game or category to save with the quote. Empty = whatever your streaming site last reported.

variables.success: True if the quote was saved
variables.quoteCount: How many quotes there are now

quotes.delete.description: Deletes a saved quote by its number. Good for a mod-only !delquote command.

fields.id: The quote's number, like 12 or #12. The default %input0% is the first word a viewer typed after the command.

variables.success: True if the quote existed and was deleted

quotes.edit.description: Changes a saved quote: its text, who said it, or its game. Anything you leave empty stays as it was.

fields.id: The quote's number, like 12 or #12. The default %input0% is the first word a viewer typed after the command.
fields.text: The new text. Empty keeps the old text.
fields.user: The new speaker. Empty keeps the old one.
fields.game: The new game or category. Empty keeps the old one.

variables.quoteUpdated: True if the quote was found and changed

quotes.get.description: Looks up a saved quote and puts it in variables so you can say it in chat. Give a number for a certain quote, or leave it empty for a random one.

fields.id: The quote's number, like 12 or #12. Empty, or not a number, picks a random quote. The default %input0% is the first word after the command.
fields.search: Only for random: pick only from quotes that contain this text, user or game, like "minecraft". Empty = any quote.
fields.fireShown: Tick to also start actions with the "Quote shown" trigger. Untick to read the quote quietly.

variables.quoteFound: True if a quote was found
variables.quoteGame: The game or category at the time

quotes.count.description: Counts your saved quotes and puts the number in a variable.

store.review.description: Approves a points store purchase that waits for you, or rejects it and gives the points back. Good for a mod button or a chat command.

fields.mode: Approve = the viewer gets what they bought. Reject = turn it down and give the points back.
fields.redemption: Which purchase, by its id. Empty = the oldest purchase that is still waiting.

variables.success: True if a waiting purchase was found and handled

store.setItem.description: Changes a points store item: switch it on or off, or change how many are left. Good for selling a limited item only at certain times.

fields.item: The item's name, exactly as in your store.
fields.enabled: Keep = leave as it is. Enable = viewers can buy it. Disable = hide it. Toggle = switch to the opposite.
fields.stock: How many are left. Empty keeps it. 10 sets it to 10. +5 adds five, -5 takes five away. -1 means unlimited.

variables.itemEnabled: True if the item can be bought now
variables.itemStock: How many are left (-1 means unlimited)

points.add.description: Gives points to a viewer, like a reward for a trivia win. Points are your channel currency that viewers collect.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name. Empty = whoever started the action. Viewers must have chatted before.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.amount: How many points to give, a whole number like 100.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.
fields.applyMultipliers: Tick to give more (or less) points if the viewer or their group has a points multiplier.
fields.destination: Optional. A variable to also receive their new total, without % signs, like userPoints. Empty = only %points%.

variables.points: The viewer's total after the change
variables.pointsAdded: How many points were really given

points.awardAll.description: Gives points to every viewer Cuebot knows, or only to those who are around. Good for a "free points for everyone" moment.

fields.platform: Only give to viewers on this site. Empty = every site.
fields.amount: How many points each viewer gets, a whole number like 10.
fields.onlyActive: Tick to give only to viewers who chatted recently, not to everyone Cuebot has ever seen.
fields.applyMultipliers: Tick to give more (or less) points to viewers or groups with a points multiplier.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

points.awardGroup.description: Gives points to every viewer in a group, like "VIPs". Groups are made on the Users & Groups page.

fields.amount: How many points each member gets, a whole number like 10.
fields.applyMultipliers: Tick to give more (or less) points to viewers or groups with a points multiplier.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

points.awardPresent.description: Gives points to every viewer who chatted recently. Good for a "thanks for being here" bonus.

fields.platform: Only give to viewers on this site. Empty = every site.
fields.amount: How many points each viewer gets, a whole number like 10.
fields.applyMultipliers: Tick to give more (or less) points to viewers or groups with a points multiplier.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

points.check.description: Checks if a viewer has enough points, then runs the Enough steps if yes or the Not enough steps if no. It takes no points. Good before a paid action.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name. Empty = whoever started the action. Viewers must have chatted before.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.amount: How many points are needed, a whole number like 100.
fields.breakOnFailure: Tick to stop the whole action when they do not have enough. Untick to run the Not enough steps instead.
fields.destination: A variable to also receive their total, without % signs. The default userPoints means you can use %userPoints%.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.pointsMissing: How many more points they need (0 if enough)

points.delete.description: Removes a viewer from the points list completely, as if they never had any. Use "Reset user points" if you only want zero.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name. Empty = whoever started the action. Viewers must have chatted before.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.pointsDeleted: True if they had points that were deleted

points.get.description: Looks up how many points a viewer has and puts it in a variable. Good for a !points command that tells chat their total.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name. The default %input0% is the first word after the command. Empty = whoever started the action.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.pointsFormatted: The total with the points name, like 500 Coins
variables.pointsRank: Their place in the points ranking (1 = first)

points.getDefinition.description: Reads how a points currency is set up (its name, symbol and so on) and saves it in variables. Mostly for advanced uses.

fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.
fields.variable: The start of the variable names, without % signs. The default pointsDefinition gives %pointsDefinition.name% and more.

variables.pointsDefinition.name: The name of the points (the start can be changed in the settings)
variables.pointsDefinition.singularName: The name for one point, like Coin

points.leaderboard.description: Builds the top list of viewers with the most points, as text for chat and as variables. Good for a !top command.

fields.count: How many viewers to list, like 5.
fields.offset: How many places to skip. 0 starts at first place, 5 starts at sixth.
fields.platform: Only list viewers on this site. Empty = every site.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.leaderboard: The list as one line, like "1. Kris (500 Coins), 2. Sam (400 Coins)"
variables.leaderboardCount: How many viewers are in the list
variables.leaderboard1User: The name of first place (leaderboard2User is second, and so on)
variables.leaderboard1Points: The points of first place (leaderboard2Points is second, and so on)

points.getMultiplier.description: Looks up how fast a viewer earns points. 1 is normal, 2 is double. Their group can change it too.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name. Empty = whoever started the action. Viewers must have chatted before.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.pointsMultiplier: How fast they earn points in all (1 = normal)
variables.pointsUserMultiplier: The multiplier set just for them (1 if none)

points.remove.description: Takes points away from a viewer. Their total never goes below 0. Use "all" to empty their balance.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name. Empty = whoever started the action. Viewers must have chatted before.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.amount: How many points to take, a whole number like 50, or the word all. Their total never goes below 0.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.points: The viewer's total after the change
variables.pointsRemoved: How many points were really taken

points.resetAll.description: Sets everyone's points back to zero. Be careful: this cannot be undone. Good for a fresh start each season.

fields.platform: Only reset viewers on this site. Empty = every site.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

points.resetUser.description: Sets one viewer's points back to zero. The viewer stays in the list. Use "Delete user points" to remove them completely.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name. Empty = whoever started the action. Viewers must have chatted before.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.destination: A variable to also receive their new total, without % signs. The default userPoints means you can use %userPoints%.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.points: The viewer's total after the reset (0)

points.setGroupMultiplier.description: Makes everyone in a group earn points faster or slower, like 2 for double. Good for rewarding "Subscribers" or "VIPs".

fields.multiplier: How much faster, like 2 for double or 1.5 for one and a half times. Empty removes the group's multiplier.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

points.set.description: Sets a viewer's points to exactly a number, no matter how many they had before. Use "Add points" to give extra instead.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name. Empty = whoever started the action. Viewers must have chatted before.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.amount: The new total, a whole number like 500.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.points: The viewer's total after the change

points.setUserMultiplier.description: Makes one viewer earn points faster or slower, like 2 for double. Good as a special thank-you for a supporter.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name. Empty = whoever started the action. Viewers must have chatted before.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.multiplier: How much faster, like 2 for double or 1.5 for one and a half times. Empty removes their multiplier.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.pointsMultiplier: How fast they earn points in all now

points.spend.description: Charges a viewer points, if they have enough. It runs the Paid steps if it worked or the Not enough steps if they were too poor. Good for paid commands.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name. Empty = whoever started the action. Viewers must have chatted before.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.amount: How many points it costs, a whole number like 100, or the word all.
fields.stopIfNotEnough: Tick to stop the whole action when they cannot pay. Untick to run the Not enough steps instead.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.points: The viewer's total after the payment
variables.pointsMissing: How many more points they would have needed (0 if paid)

points.transfer.description: Moves points from one viewer to another, like a !give command. It runs the Transferred steps if it worked or the Failed steps if not.

fields.platform: The site the giver is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userName: The giver's chat name. Empty = whoever started the action.
fields.userId: Optional. The giver's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.toUserName: Who gets the points. The default %input0% is the first word after the command, like !give kris 50.
fields.toUserId: Optional. The receiver's id on their site. If given, it is used instead of the name.
fields.toPlatform: The site the receiver is on. Empty = the same site as the giver.
fields.amount: How many points to give. The default %input1% is the second word after the command. A whole number, or the word all.
fields.currency: The name of the points, like "Coins". Empty = your normal points.

variables.points: The giver's total after the transfer
variables.targetPoints: The receiver's total after the transfer
variables.pointsError: If it failed: the reason, like "not enough points"
